thread:
incidents-bot: ALERT — spike in 502s and CB timeouts for route /v1/generate (svc: runtime-prod, region: us-west-2). Detector: contbatch-guardrails. 60s window: 430 errors (baseline 2.1/s).

olivia: I'm on it. paging @samir (oncall) and @maya (sre) — marking P1. Any known deploys in the last 30m? :rotating_light:

samir: I wasn't on deploys. jumping in. seeing a huge jump in cont-batch timeouts and KV eviction rate. attaching quick metrics snapshot.

samir: logs (truncated):
```
2026-03-15T14:22:01Z runtime[pool-3]: contbatch: seq_id=abcd123 tokens=10240 max_batch_tokens=8192 -> timeout
2026-03-15T14:22:02Z runtime[pool-3]: kvcache: eviction_count=12456 delta=+980
2026-03-15T14:22:03Z runtime[pool-3]: request=client=acme-payments status=502 latency=1500ms reason=cb_timeout
```

maya: interesting — eviction_count jump suggests we hit threshold and started thrashing pages into storage, which increases latency and triggers CB timeouts. any recent config changes to max_batch_tokens / max_num_seqs?

ricardo: There was a config push 14:10 that changed the new default batching policy for smaller models: max_batch_tokens lowered from 12288 -> 8192 and max_num_seqs from 128 -> 96 to reduce VRAM tail. The change was gated but applied cluster-wide for runtime-prod.

olivia: that seems like the root cause — lowering batch token limit increased contention for KV cache pages, causing evictions and higher service time per token. customers with long-context workloads (acme-payments, ledgerx) hit 502s.

samir: mitigation plan proposal: 1) rollback the cluster-wide batching policy to previous values OR 2) patch runtime to increase max_batch_tokens for high-throughput routes and temporarily disable continuous batching for the worst-hit routes. prefer option 2 for minimal blast radius.

olivia: agree go with option 2. Samir, you do the hotfix, Maya watch metrics and hold. I'll notify support to surface impacted customers.

samir: doing a scoped patch now — targeting route tag: route=/v1/generate tenant=acme-payments and global fallback for routes with high average seq_len>1024.

samir: patch command:
```
# runtime-admin is internal service to update per-route batching policy
curl -X POST "https://runtime-admin.internal/api/v1/batching/patch" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","tenant":"acme-payments","patch":{"max_batch_tokens":12288,"max_num_seqs":128,"continuous_batching_enabled":false}}'
```

ops-bridge-bot: Bridge created — https://ops.redwood/bridges/BRG-4271 (participants: olivia, samir, maya, ricardo).

samir: applied patch to acme-payments route at 14:33. checking immediate effects.

maya: metrics: evictions down 70% in 60s for that route, CB timeouts trending down. overall 502 rate for runtime-prod decreased from 7.2/s -> 1.4/s.

olivia: great. can we roll similar per-route patches for ledgerx and internal-batch-test? prioritize tenants with >1% error-rate.

samir: applying bulk patch for top-10 affected tenants now with a script. script snippet: 
```
for t in acme-payments ledgerx corp-pay; do
  curl -s -X POST https://runtime-admin.internal/api/v1/batching/patch \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
    -d "{\"tenant\":\"$t\",\"patch\":{\"max_batch_tokens\":12288,\"max_num_seqs\":128,\"continuous_batching_enabled\":false}}"
done
```

ricardo: FYI: this will raise memory usage on some nodes. we should monitor OOMs. I've queued an autoscale policy bump to add 4 nodes in us-west-2 for the next 30m.

maya: watching OOM/eviction/latency dashboards. also flipped a temporary rate-limit for anonymous traffic to reduce tail load: `rl:anon=300r/s`

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — P1: contbatch threshold mismatch. Status: mitigation in progress. Customer-impact: partial (some tenants experienced 502s and high latency). Next update in 10m.

olivia: support note drafted, will send to customers impacted (acme-payments, ledgerx) with ETA for fix and mitigation steps. Samir, please add a comment in the bridge with the exact timestamps of patches.

samir: done — patches at 2165431980..2165432030, bulk at 2165432085. Observed error rate drop ~14:36.

maya: tail latency 95th percentile across runtime-prod back to normal ranges. still seeing sporadic timeouts from one node (runtime-node-77). ricardo can you take node-77 out of rotation and collect heap dump?

ricardo: node-77 drained and heap dump collected. dump shows high page faulting with lots of cold KV pages being loaded. I pushed a targeted k8s taint to prevent scheduling.

olivia: customer comms sent (support thread id SUP-9982). we published a status page update: "Degraded — continuous batching timeouts causing partial 502s; mitigations applied; fix in progress."

incidents-bot: ACTIONS (recorded):
- roll-back global lower batch token change OR make it opt-in per-route (owner: product-config)
- add canary gates to batching policy pushes (owner: eng-releases)
- improve alerting to correlate kvcache eviction spikes with contbatch timeouts (owner: eng-sre)
- postmortem owner: olivia, due 72h

olivia: marking postmortem owner and will kick off postmortem doc after bridge closes. thanks everyone. final note: we should consider adding an emergency override to instantly disable continuous batching cluster-wide for 60s while we triage.

samir: creating a short-lived feature flag: `cb_emergency_disable` with TTL=60s. deploying now.

samir: emergency flag applied at 14:48, global continuous batching suppressed for 60s. watching for regressions.

maya: 502 rate stable at baseline. closing bridge, moving to monitoring.

ops-bridge-bot: Bridge BRG-4271 closed by olivia.

olivia: thanks — follow-ups synced in the bridge and ops board. I'll schedule the 72h postmortem invite. :calendar: 

samir: TL;DR root cause: config push lowered max_batch_tokens/max_num_seqs cluster-wide. That change interacted poorly with high-context tenant workloads, causing KV cache churn and contbatch timeouts. Hotfix: per-tenant patch to restore higher batch limits + temporary disable continuous batching on affected routes; autoscale to relieve pressure.

maya: will add correlation dashboards and a composite alert that triggers when (kvcache_evictions > X) AND (contbatch_timeouts > Y) AND (500s_rate > Z).

olivia: closing thread. moving to postmortem. thanks all. :seedling:
